status: Original proposed implications preserved and namespaced; not all are adopted or independent evidence

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md: familiar exact words; precise technical terminology; reader edit
proposal.trigger: A real unfamiliar or mixed-knowledge intended audience and a term whose interpretation is consequential.
proposal.candidate: Present a task-relevant technical term with the needed explanation in natural context or offer a more familiar accurate formulation; test both for the actual readers.
proposal.benefit: May reduce avoidable subjective difficulty while preserving technical distinctions.
proposal.counterexample: In specialist documentation, an exact established term can be more fluent and unambiguous than a vague paraphrase.
proposal.mechanical: Record audience, declared terms and known glossary references; identify exact term occurrences only.
proposal.semantic: Decide whether the audience needs explanation, whether substitutes preserve meaning and whether scope remains accurate.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/references/language-and-meaning.md: place brief definition naturally near the term
proposal.trigger: Definitions or optional glosses are introduced for readers new to a domain.
proposal.candidate: Assess visibility and use of definition in the reading flow; do not presume mere optional availability establishes comprehension.
proposal.benefit: Avoids a false completeness claim from existence of a glossary or hover.
proposal.counterexample: A trained audience may not need an inline definition; mouseover failure cannot establish that inline teaching fails.
proposal.mechanical: Check that supplied glossary entry and term link exist; log availability, not whether it was read.
proposal.semantic: Judge context, comprehensibility, precision and readers’ needs; measure uptake and comprehension separately.

proposal.existing_rule: accepted-foundations.md F01–F06; edit-with-purpose/SKILL.md no automatic shortness
proposal.trigger: Reading metrics or engagement data are considered for revisions.
proposal.candidate: Treat readability indices and length as descriptive diagnostics scoped to audience and form; do not translate a score into a grade requirement or optimize engagement by default.
proposal.benefit: Makes tradeoffs visible without silently replacing author purpose.
proposal.counterexample: A longer precise term or a longer complete explanation may be more accessible than a shorter obscure alternative.
proposal.mechanical: Compute length or formula with stated tokenizer and word list; record source and scope.
proposal.semantic: Evaluate familiarity, goal alignment, accuracy and reader benefit; models cannot infer these from a numeric score.

proposal.existing_rule: write-with-purpose/SKILL.md and language-and-meaning.md preserve uncertainty, qualifications, precision and voice
proposal.trigger: A bundled style recipe advises removing hedges, acronyms or making particular punctuation mandatory.
proposal.candidate: Reject component quotas; evaluate each qualification against evidence and preserve when it changes supported certainty or scope.
proposal.benefit: Avoids producing a confident but stronger or misleading claim.
proposal.counterexample: A statistically warranted possibility cannot become a certainty to imitate a low-hedge experimental condition.
proposal.mechanical: Flag changed modal/negation or removed declared term for review, with false positives.
proposal.semantic: Decide evidentiary force and meaning before approving edit.

proposal.existing_rule: rule-calibration report; Astra candidate decision procedure; accepted F09 and measurement separation
proposal.trigger: Testing whether audience-aware assistance improves writing.
proposal.candidate: Run held-out audience-matched comparison with independent semantic fidelity, author acceptance and comprehension tests; separate readability feelings from performance and engagement.
proposal.benefit: Could test a differentiator in preserving nuanced content while adapting to actual readers.
proposal.counterexample: A satisfying, fluent output may omit a key qualification or be factually wrong.
proposal.mechanical: Blind and log assigned version, source IDs, decision status, data splits and score calculations.
proposal.semantic: Independent review of content, attribution, author authority and response quality.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md reader question and reasons
proposal.trigger: Author requests response to known viewpoint
proposal.benefit: Retain audience and specific claim context for author review
proposal.mechanical: Store supplied claim, audience and source target separately
proposal.semantic: Judge whether reply engages claim fairly and appropriately
proposal.counterexample: Personal exploration without a known opposing claim needs no opponent record

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md; skills/edit-with-purpose/references/plain-language-edit.md qualification
proposal.trigger: Uncertainty or qualification changes claim meaning
proposal.benefit: Preserve warranted uncertainty
proposal.mechanical: Locate supplied qualifier only
proposal.semantic: Judge whether qualifier is warranted and what it scopes
proposal.counterexample: Redundant hedges can obscure a fact; necessary may can prevent false certainty
proposal.evidence: P02 Table 3 pp. 6, 10 raw counts do not isolate effect

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/research/astra-rule-revision-2026-11-16.md; experiments/dataset-adoption-2026-11-16/plugin-reuse-notes.md
proposal.trigger: Context contains speakers, reply edges and targets
proposal.benefit: Keep author, addressee and referenced claim distinguishable
proposal.mechanical: Preserve source-provided IDs, reply edge, spans and unknowns
proposal.semantic: Determine actual actor, addressee, function and relation target in context
proposal.counterexample: Quoted you addresses a character rather than the reader
proposal.evidence: P02 pp. 3–6; reply edge is not function gold

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/accepted-foundations.md
proposal.trigger: An automatic system proposes optimizing delta proxy
proposal.benefit: Protect author intent, evidence, voice and semantic accuracy
proposal.mechanical: Retain count as descriptive only if task relevant
proposal.semantic: Assess whether words, links and emphasis serve actual intent
proposal.counterexample: Technical explanation must preserve a term; safety warning may require urgency

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md: organize around reader question and select evidence; references/concepts-and-claims.md: distinguish proposal from evidence
proposal.trigger: Author requests a proposal or decision memo and its purpose, audience and source material are available.
proposal.mechanical: Track supplied claim-to-source links and unfilled claim-evidence slots, labeled unresolved when extraction is uncertain.
proposal.judgment: Assess whether rationale, material benefits, costs, risks and actionable request are supported and relevant; preserve truthful positive emphasis and author choice.
proposal.benefit: Make merit and consequences legible without generic promotional phrases.
proposal.counterexample: A speculative concept may validly state a hoped-for benefit if explicitly marked as a hypothesis; no mandate to supply absent facts.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/references/language-and-meaning.md: preserve uncertainty and force; edit-with-purpose/SKILL.md: preserve source context
proposal.trigger: A proposed edit strengthens novelty, confidence, causal direction, certainty, comparative claims or commitments.
proposal.mechanical: Highlight changed modal, negation, number, comparative and superlative tokens as review candidates; do not decide entailment by token matching.
proposal.judgment: Compare full claim, context and underlying source, retain warranted qualifiers; allow genuinely supported assertive wording and accurate adjectives.
proposal.benefit: Support persuasive emphasis without making claims stronger than their evidence.
proposal.counterexample: Replacing an unnecessarily tentative assertion with a stronger one can be valid if the supplied source actually supports it.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md: keep technical terms and avoid uniform sentence-length preference
proposal.trigger: A sentence is difficult for the intended reader or hides a relevant relation in a proposal or memo.
proposal.mechanical: Flag only declared word limits and optionally show observed word/sentence counts without a target.
proposal.judgment: Compare alternatives for recoverable meaning, technical precision, audience needs and rhythm; preserve complexity necessary for the argument.
proposal.benefit: Improve explanation while retaining technical substance and voice.
proposal.counterexample: A specialist evaluator may need a precise technical term and a multi-clause qualification.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/accepted-foundations.md: Family → Form → Section; features are observations, not targets
proposal.trigger: Reviewing decision-oriented forms with author-supplied purpose and evidence.
proposal.mechanical: Show optional checklist slots for decision, options and support only when explicitly requested or required.
proposal.judgment: Check whether proposed action, alternatives and consequences are understandable for this decision; do not require fixed sequence or all slots.
proposal.benefit: Possible form-sensitive support and comparison, not demonstrated funding advantage.
proposal.counterexample: A short memo may legitimately address one narrow decision with alternatives linked separately.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/references/structure-and-purpose.md: choose material for contribution, consider reader question; accepted-foundations F02
proposal.trigger: Author requests a title or heading for a known form, audience and destination.
proposal.action: Compare whether each candidate names the contribution and gives the intended reader enough orientation; allow justified intrigue, interrogative framing or ambiguity.
proposal.expected_benefit: Contextual title review without a single algorithmic concreteness optimum.
proposal.counterexample: A reflective essay title may deliberately leave the meaning open until the ending; an API reference heading may need exact identifier.
proposal.mechanical: Check declared title limits, presence/consistency of explicit terms and heading structure.
proposal.semantic: Judge fidelity, reader expectations, justified omissions and voice with author.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md: author intent and voice, source fidelity; accepted-foundations preserve originality
proposal.trigger: Attention-oriented suggestion changes specificity, affect, or promises.
proposal.action: Review whether the title truthfully reflects the piece and the authors intended framing; do not insert negativity or omit material facts merely for CTR.
proposal.expected_benefit: Protect source fidelity and author control.
proposal.counterexample: A naturally negative title is appropriate when it faithfully describes an adverse event.
proposal.mechanical: Detect mismatched named items only with supplied canonical records; check declared constraints.
proposal.semantic: Evaluate framing, emotional accuracy, fairness and relevance in full context.

proposal.existing_rule: write-with-purpose: avoid generic preference for fewer words or uniformly short sentences; no default readability grade
proposal.trigger: A tool proposes mandatory brevity, a readability score, preferred pronoun or negative wording.
proposal.action: Do not use lexical signals as universal pass/fail rules.
proposal.expected_benefit: Preserve necessary technical vocabulary, voice and functional variation.
proposal.counterexample: A publisher can set an actual character ceiling; a title can be misleadingly long or short regardless of score.
proposal.mechanical: Count words or characters only under declared measurement rules and enforce explicit limits.
proposal.semantic: Reader comprehension and faithful tone require assessment.

proposal.existing_rule: dataset-adoption plugin-reuse-notes: separate purpose, form, provenance and semantic review; calibration report indicates low function agreement
proposal.trigger: When a user asks the plugin to compare title options for a specific intended audience.
proposal.action: Offer author-chosen alternatives with stated reader question, tradeoffs and uncertainty; evaluate actual readers against intended outcomes, not just clicks.
proposal.expected_benefit: Plausible differentiation through source-grounded, author-controlled choice.
proposal.counterexample: A narrow copy-edit needs no title generation, ranking or testing workflow.
proposal.mechanical: Store candidate versions, constraints and exact source links; evaluate experimental units and outcome definitions.
proposal.semantic: Author decides voice and goal; blinded reader task and preregistered comparison needed to demonstrate usefulness.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md; references/cole-lyons-style.md; docs/writing-harness/paragraph-functions.json narrate/illustrate
proposal.scope_trigger: Author supplies a relevant experience or a concrete example advances the stated purpose.
proposal.proposal: Offer a sourced scene or example as one optional route, preserving origin and distinguishing observation from invention; never require a narrative opening.
proposal.expected_benefit: Makes an abstract relationship recoverable while preserving choice and voice; benefit remains to be tested for this audience.
proposal.counterexample: A technical reference entry needs a precise definition or lookup, not an invented story.
proposal.mechanical: Record provenance, author approval, and links to the illustrated claim.
proposal.semantic_or_author: Whether the case illuminates the point and the author wants its tone.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md; skills/edit-with-purpose/SKILL.md; references/language-and-meaning.md
proposal.scope_trigger: A revision changes tense, reference, article, preposition, modality or attribution.
proposal.proposal: Protect temporal state, scope, actor and technical meaning; show alternatives rather than optimizing pronouns, grammatical word counts or tense for citation prediction.
proposal.expected_benefit: Preserve factual meaning and author voice while giving agency and temporal framing contextual attention.
proposal.counterexample: Changing had to has can imply continued relevance or a different time relationship; removing a preposition can lose a condition.
proposal.mechanical: Compare tokens and declared preserved phrases; flag changes to protected terms and tense as review candidates, not errors.
proposal.semantic_or_author: Determine whether meaning changes, and whether chosen voice serves the task.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/paragraph-functions.json support/interpret; skills/write-with-purpose/references/structure-and-purpose.md
proposal.scope_trigger: A claim, example, evidence or inference is present.
proposal.proposal: Retain target links and ask whether the evidence supports the particular claim and whether inference exceeds it.
proposal.expected_benefit: Supports source fidelity and meaningful connected reasoning.
proposal.counterexample: A highly shared emotional anecdote may illustrate experience but cannot establish population frequency or prove a claim.
proposal.mechanical: Check links and provenance fields resolve; count only supplied annotated evidence.
proposal.semantic_or_author: Judge evidential relevance, inferential scope and whether explanation helps reader.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md; accepted-foundations.md F05/F06/F09
proposal.scope_trigger: A tool proposes changing prose to maximize sharing, citation counts, sentiment or low readability score.
proposal.proposal: Treat these as optional user-declared outcomes with testable tradeoffs, not proxies for good writing, comprehension or accuracy.
proposal.expected_benefit: Avoids sacrificing meaning, learning goals and voice for an indirect popularity measure.
proposal.counterexample: A safety notice may rightly express low-arousal uncertainty and specialist terminology while serving its audience.
proposal.mechanical: Record declared purpose and inspect counts as descriptive data only.
proposal.semantic_or_author: Author chooses objectives; reader studies measure comprehension or task success directly.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/references/structure-and-purpose.md: For a decision or operational explanation, make the choice, reasons and consequences recoverable.
proposal.trigger: Actual decision work with an audience and a live choice
proposal.change: Offer optional blank prompts for decision, observations, decision criteria/warrant, interpretation, alternatives and constraints. Ask only for relevant information; author chooses sequence and completeness.
proposal.benefit: Makes the recommendation’s connection to evidence reviewable.
proposal.counterexample: A status-only sales report may legitimately have no explicit recommendation; an implicit one must not be invented.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/accepted-foundations.md: Family → Form → Section; section need not have a heading; preserve variation.
proposal.trigger: Author requests outline for an empirical article or comparable evidence-backed report
proposal.change: Show section jobs and optional alternative arrangements, with blends and recursion allowed; classify sections from purpose plus context rather than heading.
proposal.benefit: Offers reusable options without flattening discipline-specific practices.
proposal.counterexample: A section called Results can include interpretations and an unheaded Introduction can orient.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/paragraph-functions.json: assert/support/interpret/compare/qualify and explicit relations
proposal.trigger: Draft contains recommendation and potential reasons
proposal.change: Independently note recommendation, evidence, warrant, attribution and any relation target; prompt for a missing link only when contextual review finds one needed.
proposal.benefit: Supports examination of the inference instead of treating one label as another.
proposal.counterexample: A bare citation, juxtaposition or claim that a warrant is implicit does not demonstrate actual support.

proposal.existing_rule: experiments/rule-calibration-2026-11-16/report.md: no demonstrated agreement improvement; evidence anchors are not full realization spans.
proposal.trigger: Imported sentence or phrase roles mapped to paragraph functions
proposal.change: Keep original source labels and overlapping spans, separate evidence anchors and complete realization spans, preserve uncertain and multiple readings, and run a fresh independent boundary study.
proposal.benefit: Makes disagreements inspectable and prevents unit conversion from manufacturing certainty.
proposal.counterexample: Cotos ICC on a different unit and scheme does not establish improved exact-set agreement on our 36 paragraphs.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/edit-with-purpose/SKILL.md: preserve effective wording and apply smallest targeted change.
proposal.trigger: Author asks for Methods section planning or structural review
proposal.change: Offer context/design; study/data, tools and procedures; data preparation/analysis and reasons as optional questions, not required sections or draft language.
proposal.benefit: Prompts recoverable reporting and design rationale in suitable empirical studies.
proposal.counterexample: A theoretical paper, a procedure, or a business report can legitimately lack the full experimental Methods structure.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/paragraph-functions.json guidance; experiments/rule-calibration-2026-11-16/report.md
proposal.trigger: Multiple defensible functions on a shared text unit
proposal.proposal: Preserve multiple labels and distinguish exact full-set, overlap-sensitive set distance and per-label positive agreement, with raw coder sets and denominators. Evaluate mv-alpha on comparable pre-specified shared units and separately inspect boundaries; do not force primary function.
proposal.benefit: Makes strict-subset errors and sparse shared absences visible.
proposal.counterexample: Two coders may assign identical sets but point to different claims or realization spans; agreement does not prove either interpretation correct.
proposal.mechanical_vs_semantic: Set comparisons and offset checks mechanical; label and target validity semantic; author retains final editorial control.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/research/astra-rule-revision-2026-11-16.md; calibration report
proposal.trigger: Relations such as support or qualification, or function-length calculation
proposal.proposal: Retain targets, evidence anchors and complete realization spans as separate fields, including discontinuity and uncollected/uncertain status. Compare target unit, target span and semantic adequacy separately; anchor text alone does not establish realization length.
proposal.benefit: Shows why same function set can still disagree about its target; prevents invalid function-length measurements.
proposal.counterexample: An illustrative sentence with no explicit support target need not be coded as supporting a claim.
proposal.mechanical_vs_semantic: Hash, source offsets and target existence are mechanical; scope, sufficiency and relation meaning require review.
proposal.evidence: P18 p. 7 sentence unitization; calibration report target overlap and anchor limitation.

proposal.existing_rule: experiments/rule-calibration-2026-11-16/report.md
proposal.trigger: Planning a new independent coding pilot
proposal.proposal: Freeze codebook, train with held-out examples, report coder identity/experience, sampling, all set counts, prevalence, target judgments, missing/unresolved state and pre-adjudication results. Test boundary agreement independently. Select any future decision criterion in advance; do not apply 750 as a threshold.
proposal.benefit: Makes disagreement diagnosis and independent replication feasible.
proposal.counterexample: High agreement can result from both coders omitting a function or using shared blank labels; adjudication alone is not accuracy.
proposal.mechanical_vs_semantic: Completeness and provenance checks mechanical; category meaning and adjudication judged with context.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/edit-with-purpose/SKILL.md; skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md; accepted-foundations F01 F04 F05
proposal.trigger: Assessing length or cutting prose
proposal.proposal: Use counts as descriptive signals and author-specified limits; judge necessity, connection and reader task before cutting. No general shortness, lengthening, or citation-maximization rule.
proposal.benefit: Preserves needed explanation and respects actual constraints.
proposal.counterexample: A strict abstract word limit may require a shorter version despite positive length-citation associations.
proposal.mechanical_vs_semantic: Count explicit budgets mechanically; decide necessary content and reader comprehension by review.
proposal.evidence: P14 pp. 1–4; correlation does not establish comprehension.

proposal.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md; skills/edit-with-purpose/references/plain-language-edit.md
proposal.trigger: Technical terms, modifiers, tense and qualifications
proposal.proposal: Protect accurate terms and uncertainty; choose tense by chronology, modifiers by meaning, explanation by audience. Do not automate broad deletion or insertion of hedges, adjectives or superlatives.
proposal.benefit: Avoids distorted claims and permits author voice.
proposal.counterexample: Unexplained specialist terminology may require a brief definition for a novice even though rarer terms correlate with citations.
proposal.mechanical_vs_semantic: Detect candidate tense or terms mechanically; appropriateness, accuracy and reader knowledge require judgment.
proposal.evidence: P14 pp. 2–3; keyword and frequency proxies not comprehension tests.

proposal.existing_rule: docs/writing-harness/paragraph-functions.json support and qualify; accepted-foundations F07 F09
proposal.trigger: Abstract claims about novelty, evidence, significance or uncertainty
proposal.proposal: Treat novelty words and hedges only as prompts to review factual basis, affected claim and scope; never assert significance, increase confidence or remove qualification merely to optimize citations.
proposal.benefit: Separates lexical cues from evidence-grounded rhetorical function.
proposal.counterexample: A well-grounded novel result may accurately say novel; a word alone does not establish novelty.
proposal.mechanical_vs_semantic: Find cue words mechanically; verifying novelty and support is semantic and evidence-based.
